panels.title: Active WAN — Traffic

targets.query:
activeIfaces = from(bucket: "rvtc")
  |> range(start: -2m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "mikrotik_interface" and r._field == "ifOperStatus")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.ifDescr == "rogers-wan" or r.ifDescr == "starlink-wan")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._value == 1)
  |> last()
  |> distinct(column: "ifDescr")
  |> findColumn(fn: (key) => true, column: "ifDescr")

from(bucket: "rvtc")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "mikrotik_interface")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "ifInOctets" or r._field == "ifOutOctets")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => contains(value: r.ifDescr, set: activeIfaces))
  |> derivative(unit: 1s, nonNegative: true)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with _value: r._value * 8.0 }))

panels.description: Automatically follows whichever WAN interface currently has an up link — shows In/Out bits/sec for that interface only. If neither is up, shows the 'not connected' message instead of an empty/flat graph.

  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "synology_nas")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "system_temperature" or r._field == "disk1_temperature")

from(bucket: "rvtc")
  |> range(start: -5m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "synology_volume")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "volume_used_bytes" or r._field == "volume_total_bytes")

panels.title: NAS SMART Attributes (failure-predictive only)

targets.query:
from(bucket: "rvtc")
  |> range(start: -5m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "synology_smart")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.attribute_name == "Reallocated_Sector_Ct" or r.attribute_name == "Current_Pending_Sector" or r.attribute_name == "Offline_Uncorrectable" or r.attribute_name == "Reallocated_Event_Count" or r.attribute_name == "UDMA_CRC_Error_Count")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "attribute_value" or r._field == "attribute_status" or r._field == "attribute_raw")
  |> last()
  |> pivot(rowKey:["_time","attribute_name"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> group()
  |> keep(columns: ["attribute_name", "attribute_value", "attribute_raw", "attribute_status"])
  |> sort(columns: ["attribute_name"])

panels.description: Only the SMART attributes that actually predict drive failure — a rising raw count on any of these (especially Reallocated_Sector_Ct or Current_Pending_Sector) is the thing worth acting on. Everything else in the full attribute set is informational noise, not omitted by accident.

panels.title: Network Detail — Both WAN Interfaces Overlaid
WAN Traffic — rogers-wan / starlink-wan (both, historical)

targets.query:
from(bucket: "rvtc")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "mikrotik_interface")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.ifDescr == "rogers-wan" or r.ifDescr == "starlink-wan")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "ifInOctets" or r._field == "ifOutOctets")
  |> derivative(unit: 1s, nonNegative: true)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with _value: r._value * 8.0 }))

panels.description: Both interfaces plotted together regardless of current status — useful for reviewing a past failover event (e.g. seeing exactly when traffic moved from one WAN to the other).
